newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Radical Indonesia group calls for Timor pullout.
newsitem.headline: Radical Indonesia group calls for Timor pullout.

text.p: A radical Indonesian students group on Saturday called on Jakarta to withdraw its troops from East Timor and hold a referendum on the future of the former Portuguese colony.

The People's Democratic Party (PRD), which has been blamed for riots in Jakarta in July and whose members are underground or in custody, said in a statement sent to Reuters that it supported statements by Nobel laureate Bishop Carlos Belo in which he reportedly said Indonesia had treated East Timorese like "scabby dogs" and "slaves."
Belo, who was jointly awarded the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize along with self-exiled East Timor resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta, has said he was misquoted.

"The PRD demands the New Order regime soon withdraw its military forces from East Timor and surrender (the territory) to a multi-national peacekeeping force like what was done in Bosnia, Cambodia and Ethiopia," the PRD statement said.
The New Order is the name given to the administration of President Suharto, who took power in the mid-1960s.

"(We demand) soon an opening of the isolation of East Timor for journalists, human rights institutions, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), individuals, researchers and other parties who want to know about the conditions in East Timor as objectively as possible without being prohibited, warded off or censored," the statement said.

"(We demand) soon compliance with U.N. resolution No.3485/1975 to end the occupation and give full autonomy to East Timor so that a referendum can be implemented for the people of East Timor," it said.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it a year later in an act that has not been recognised by the United Nations, which still considers Portugal as the administering power.
